findings.title: Concurrent group test never joins the reader and can false-pass or hang
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon Thread at line 139 that lists groups until deletedAll is true, but the test never retains that Thread, never joins it, and never sets deletedAll in a finally block. After the deletes it sets deletedAll (line 155) and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty (line 157). The list call most likely to overlap the deletes can still be in flight, so a NullPointerException (or any other failure) is added to caughtExceptions only after the assertion and the test passes while the race is still broken. There is also no start latch and no check that a read ran during the deletes, so an empty list does not prove the bug was exercised. If any group remove() throws, deletedAll stays false and the non-daemon reader loops forever, which keeps the Surefire JVM alive and can hang the suite. Even on the success path the in-flight HTTP call continues after the test method returns and races with later tests that share this class's injected realm and admin client. Keep the Thread, signal stop in a finally, join with a timeout before asserting, and fail if the reader never overlapped the deletes.

findings.title: Null delegate is memoized by modelSupplier and count is returned as null
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount now loads the persistence delegate through modelSupplier (line 274). That supplier is a LazyModel, which invokes getGroupModel() once and then permanently returns the same result, including null. The previous code called getGroupModel() directly, so a missing row was not stuck on the adapter. After a concurrent delete the cache can still hand out this GroupAdapter while the database lookup returns null; the first count call then pins modelSupplier to null for the rest of the session. Later calls on that same adapter to getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) dereference modelSupplier.get() with no null check and throw NullPointerException without querying again. The same poisoned supplier is passed into CachedGroup's lazy loaders (getAttributes, getRoleMappings, getSubGroups); those loaders treat a null model as the empty fallback and store it on the CachedGroup instance held in the Infinispan cache, so other sessions can see empty attributes, roles, or subgroup ids until that entry is invalidated. The method also returns null rather than a count, and GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount copies that into GroupRepresentation, so a listing that used to 500 now succeeds with subGroupCount null and any caller that unboxes the Long NPEs. Call getGroupModel() directly so a null is not cached, and return 0L when the delegate is missing.
